gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (stage III or stage IV).

candidate_evidence.quote: This is a phase I clinical study of individualized neoantigen peptide vaccine combined with targeted drugs in the treatment of EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer aimed to evaluated the safety and immune response of the neoantigen vaccine treatment.

role_evidence.quote: Patients received subcutaneous injection of individualized neoantigen peptides vaccine at a dose of 200ug per peptide once a week for 5 weeks.
First generation EGFR-TKI treatment is in progress, the treatment time is 5-6 months and there is no disease progression.

agents.drug_class_hint: first-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, ongoing background therapy, agent not named

role_evidence.quote: neoantigen vaccine + anti-angioge: neoantigen vaccine + anti-angioge

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-angiogenic targeted drug, agent not named

source_quote.quote: With EGFR-TKI sensitive mutations and no T790M.

coder_notes: NSCLC trial; glioblastoma mentioned only in brief summary as background. Only investigational agent is a personalised neoantigen peptide vaccine (excluded type). EGFR-TKI and anti-angiogenic drugs are background targeted therapy already used per label, not named. EGFR mutation is an NSCLC entry requirement linked to the background TKI, not to a candidate. Setting for NSCLC is maintenance during ongoing first-line TKI (not GBM-applicable), coded unclear.
